metadata.title: Capacitor Privacy Screen: Hide App Content
metadata.description: Add a Capacitor privacy screen to hide app content in the app switcher and block screenshots, with per-screen control, config and platform caveats.
metadata.author: Martin Donadieu
metadata.head_image_alt: Security settings illustration for adding a privacy screen to a Capacitor app
metadata.keywords: capacitor privacy screen, hide app content app switcher, capacitor prevent screenshot, FLAG_SECURE capacitor, ionic privacy screen, @capgo/capacitor-privacy-screen

faq.question: How do I hide my app content in the iOS and Android app switcher?
faq.answer: Install @capgo/capacitor-privacy-screen and call PrivacyScreen.enable(), or set enabled: true under plugins.PrivacyScreen in capacitor.config.ts. iOS shows a blur or launch screen in the snapshot, Android uses FLAG_SECURE with an optional dim or splash overlay.

faq.question: Does the privacy screen block screenshots?
faq.answer: On Android, yes. FLAG_SECURE blocks screenshots and screen recording while protection is enabled. On iOS the plugin places content in a secure rendering layer while enabled, but treat iOS screenshot blocking as best effort and never as a security boundary.

faq.question: Can I enable the privacy screen only on some pages?
faq.answer: Yes. Call enable() when entering a sensitive page and disable() when leaving it. Make sure back navigation and deep links also go through that logic.

faq.question: Does it work on the web?
faq.answer: The web implementation keeps an enabled flag for API parity, but browsers cannot hide tab previews or block screenshots.

faq.question: Does a privacy screen affect performance?
faq.answer: No measurable effect in normal use. It sets a window flag on Android and adds an overlay on iOS when the app resigns active.

blocks.text: A Capacitor privacy screen hides your app's content when the user opens the app switcher and, on Android, blocks screenshots and screen recording. Without one, iOS and Android take a snapshot of your last screen, so a bank balance, a medical record or a one-time code stays visible in the recent apps list.
adds this with one call or one config flag, and lets you protect only the screens that need it.
When a user leaves your app, both systems capture an image of the current screen:
takes a snapshot when the app resigns active and shows it in the app switcher, and briefly while the app relaunches.
shows a live or cached preview in Recents.

Anyone glancing at the phone sees that snapshot. So does anyone screen-sharing a call, or a user who records their screen for a support ticket. Screenshots are also synced to cloud photo libraries, which is where sensitive data really leaks.

Security reviews and penetration tests for these categories routinely flag missing app switcher protection. OWASP MASVS includes checks for sensitive data exposed through the UI, and auditors test exactly this.
The plugin supports Capacitor 8 with version 8.x.
